article_ideas.angle: Argue against the 'ship one great agent' pattern using the Agent Studio platform-vs-product distinction, and show what must be centralized (ontology, evals, connectors, deployment modes) versus what can be decentralized to internal teams and customers.
article_ideas.audience: AI platform engineers and enterprise product leaders
article_ideas.based_on: Agent Studio is a platform allowing both internal teams and customers to configure and build agentic products.
article_ideas.thesis: The durable asset in enterprise agentic AI is a configuration platform that lets domain users build agents under shared ontology, evaluation, and deployment constraints; individual agents are disposable artifacts of that platform.
article_ideas.title: Your Agent Platform Is the Product, Not the Agents

article_ideas.angle: Trace the path from an unconstrained document-upload workflow to ontology-constrained metadata assignment, and argue that teams that skip ontology work hit an accuracy ceiling they cannot prompt their way out of.
article_ideas.audience: Applied AI engineers and data architects
article_ideas.thesis: In regulated domains, the ontology—not prompt engineering or model choice—is the primary reliability artifact, because it converts an open generation problem into a constrained classification and retrieval problem.
article_ideas.title: Ontology First, Prompts Second: Where Agent Reliability Actually Comes From

article_ideas.angle: Decompose the timeline into administrative versus scientific time, then show why agentic gains concentrate on the administrative side and what that implies for where to invest engineering effort.
article_ideas.audience: Life-sciences technology strategists and AI product managers
article_ideas.based_on: Medable aims to reduce clinical trial timelines down to one year.
article_ideas.thesis: Compressing clinical trial timelines is mainly an automation-of-administrative-toil problem (document classification, cross-system monitoring), so the right success metrics are hours removed and escalation rates, not benchmark scores.
article_ideas.title: The 10-Year-to-1-Year Claim Is a Toil-Removal Claim, Not a Model-Quality Claim

article_ideas.angle: Reframe HITL from a product compromise to a compliance mechanism, with the FDA-auditor lookup scenario as the concrete test of whether a workflow is auditable end to end.
article_ideas.audience: Regulated-industry architects and AI governance leads
article_ideas.based_on: allowing FDA auditors to quickly find and review trial records
article_ideas.thesis: HITL checkpoints should be designed as auditable control points that produce evidence, not as fallbacks for weak models; the design question is which decisions may never be automated and how that is proven to a regulator.
article_ideas.title: Human-in-the-Loop Is a Compliance Architecture, Not an Apology

evidence_quotes.text: ETMF handles electronic trial master file documents, allowing FDA auditors to quickly find and review trial records.
the importance of human-in-the-loop design, data ontologies, and evaluation frameworks for AI agents

deep_dives.research_question: What minimum set of human-in-the-loop checkpoints and captured artifacts makes an agentic output defensible to an FDA auditor, and how does adding those checkpoints change agent throughput?
deep_dives.topic: Human-in-the-loop as a regulatory control, not a UX nicety
deep_dives.trigger_insight: the importance of human-in-the-loop design, data ontologies, and evaluation frameworks for AI agents
deep_dives.why: If the value proposition is compressing a 10-year trial timeline, every HITL gate either preserves auditability or erodes the speed claim. Quantifying that trade is the difference between a demo and a deployable regulated product.

evidence_quotes.text: ETMF processes over 80,000 documents a year per customer, requiring hours of metadata classification.
Uploading documents to ETMF and automatically assigning metadata classifications.

deep_dives.research_question: For an ontology-constrained classification agent processing tens of thousands of trial documents per customer per year, what accuracy ceiling and human-escalation rate can be achieved, and how much of the 'hours of metadata classification' is actually recoverable?
deep_dives.topic: Ontology-grounded metadata classification at document scale
deep_dives.trigger_insight: ETMF processes over 80,000 documents a year per customer, requiring hours of metadata classification.
deep_dives.why: Metadata classification is a concrete, measurable, high-volume bottleneck. If the escalation rate stays high, the agent only shifts labor rather than removing it, which invalidates the timeline-compression premise.

evidence_quotes.text: CRA agents monitor clinical research site data across 13+ different legacy systems.
CRAs navigating 13 different data source systems to monitor patient safety risks.

deep_dives.research_question: When an agent must monitor patient-safety signals spanning 13+ legacy source systems with conflicting schemas and update latencies, how should it resolve contradictions and what is the cost of being wrong?
deep_dives.topic: Agent reconciliation across fragmented legacy systems
deep_dives.trigger_insight: CRA agents monitor clinical research site data across 13+ different legacy systems.
deep_dives.why: Fragmentation across 13+ systems is the real engineering problem; the model is the easy part. Conflict-resolution policy is where agentic monitoring either earns trust or produces silent safety failures.

evidence_quotes.text: The platform allows common users and engineers to configure agents using agnostic model selection.
Supports multiple deployment patterns including top-level agent platforms and forward-deployed engineering support.

deep_dives.research_question: Can a common-user-facing configuration surface ('agnostic model selection') produce agents as reliable as hand-built ones, and what guardrails are needed so model swaps do not silently regress regulated behavior?
deep_dives.topic: Model-agnostic configuration surface for non-engineer agent builders
deep_dives.trigger_insight: The platform allows common users and engineers to configure agents using agnostic model selection.
deep_dives.why: The platform bet is that non-engineers can configure agents safely. That is falsifiable: compare configured-agent vs. engineered-agent performance and regression behavior across model swaps.

evidence_quotes.text: how they transitioned from legacy systems to agent-driven workflows

deep_dives.research_question: What does an evaluation framework look like when the ground truth is regulatory acceptability rather than task accuracy, and can it be automated enough to gate continuous deployment of agents?
deep_dives.topic: Evaluation frameworks for regulated agentic workflows
deep_dives.why: Evaluation is named as a first-class pillar of the platform alongside ontology and HITL. If evaluation cannot be expressed in regulatory terms, it cannot gate releases in a compliant environment.

project_ideas.hypothesis: Grounding an extraction/classification agent in a versioned domain ontology raises top-1 metadata accuracy by at least 15 points over an unconstrained prompt baseline at the same human-escalation budget.
project_ideas.measurement: Top-1 metadata accuracy, escalation rate, and documents-per-hour at a fixed escalation budget; falsified if the ontology variant does not beat baseline by 15 points or does not reduce escalation.
project_ideas.name: Ontology-Constrained Doc Classification Harness
project_ideas.poc: Build a small ETMF-like corpus with a versioned ontology, run (a) unconstrained prompt classification and (b) ontology-constrained classification with schema validation and escalation thresholds, then compare top-1 accuracy and escalation rate at matched throughput targets.

project_ideas.based_on: CRA agents monitor clinical research site data across 13+ different legacy systems.
project_ideas.hypothesis: An agent that maintains an explicit conflict ledger over N heterogeneous source systems surfaces patient-safety-relevant contradictions with higher recall, and fewer silent overwrites, than an agent that merges sources implicitly.
project_ideas.measurement: Contradiction recall, false-merge (silent overwrite) count, and time-to-surface per conflicting record; falsified if the ledger agent shows no recall gain or introduces more false positives than it removes.
project_ideas.name: Multi-Source Reconciliation Agent with Conflict Ledger
project_ideas.poc: Simulate 5-13 mocked legacy sources (EDC-like, site data, spreadsheets) with injected schema drift, stale timestamps, and contradictory values; run a merge-implicit agent versus a conflict-ledger agent; score contradiction detection and false-merge incidents.

project_ideas.based_on: The platform allows common users and engineers to configure agents using agnostic model selection.
project_ideas.hypothesis: Agents configured by non-engineers through an agnostic model-selection surface regress on regulated-task acceptance criteria when the underlying model is swapped, and a task-level regression suite can catch that regression before deployment.
project_ideas.measurement: Number of acceptance criteria that flip after a model swap with zero config change, and detection rate of a pre-deployment regression gate; falsified if swaps produce no measurable criteria flips.
project_ideas.name: Model-Swap Regression Gate for Configured Agents
project_ideas.poc: Author three configured agents on a fixed ontology and evaluation suite, snapshot behavior on model A, swap to model B with no config change, and diff outputs against acceptance criteria to measure silent behavioral drift.

project_ideas.hypothesis: There is an identifiable HITL checkpoint configuration that preserves near-full auditability while still removing a majority of manual document-handling hours, and beyond a small number of gates the added audit value per gate drops sharply.
project_ideas.measurement: Marginal audit-value per added gate versus marginal throughput loss; falsified if throughput loss scales linearly with gate count with no diminishing audit return.
project_ideas.name: HITL Checkpoint Throughput Trade Study
project_ideas.poc: Instrument a document-intake workflow with 0/1/3/5 HITL gates, capture the audit artifacts each produces, and measure both throughput (hours removed) and reconstructability of a decision chain from artifacts alone.

summary.html:
Overview

  • Speaker: Teresa Torres with guests Luke Bates, Jen, Piera Matthews, and Matt Schoolfield
  • Channel: Product Talk
  • Main topic: Building agentic AI systems and agent platforms at Medable to accelerate clinical trials
  • Purpose: To share how Medable built Agent Studio and utilized agentic AI to tackle complex clinical trial operations, reduce drug development timelines, and handle massive data volumes while maintaining regulatory compliance. Teresa Torres hosts a panel discussion with Medable team members Luke Bates, Jen, Piera Matthews, and Matt Schoolfield about Agent Studio, their platform for building agentic AI products. They discuss the massive administrative, regulatory, and data challenges in clinical trials, how they transitioned from legacy systems to agent-driven workflows, the importance of human-in-the-loop design, data ontologies, and evaluation frameworks for AI agents.

Topic Map

Introduction to Medable and Agent Studio

  • Explanation: Panelists introduce themselves and Medable's mission to bring effective therapies to patients faster by streamlining clinical trials.
  • Key claims:
    • It currently takes over 10 years to bring a drug to market.
    • Medable aims to reduce clinical trial timelines down to one year.
    • Agent Studio is a platform allowing both internal teams and customers to configure and build agentic products.
  • Examples:
    • Moving from 10-year clinical trials to ambitious 1-year goals.
  • Terminology:
    • Agent Studio
    • Agentic-powered solutions
    • ETMF (Electronic Trial Master File)
    • CRA (Clinical Research Associate)
  • Why it matters: Setting the scope on how agentic AI addresses deep operational bottlenecks in the multi-billion-dollar clinical trial industry.

Products Built on the Agent Platform

  • Explanation: Detailed overview of the specific products built on top of Agent Studio, including ETMF, CRA assistants, and protocol adherence tools.
  • Key claims:
    • ETMF handles electronic trial master file documents, allowing FDA auditors to quickly find and review trial records.
    • ETMF processes over 80,000 documents a year per customer, requiring hours of metadata classification.
    • CRA agents monitor clinical research site data across 13+ different legacy systems.
  • Examples:
    • Uploading documents to ETMF and automatically assigning metadata classifications.
    • CRAs navigating 13 different data source systems to monitor patient safety risks.
  • Terminology:
    • ETMF
    • CRA
    • EDC (Electronic Data Capture)
    • Ontology
  • Why it matters: Illustrates real-world applications of agentic workflows solving data fragmentation and regulatory compliance.

Platform Architecture and Deployment Patterns

  • Explanation: Explaining the technical architecture of Agent Studio, supporting agnostic models, rag knowledge, MCP connectors, workflow orchestration, and flexible deployment models.
  • Key claims:
    • The platform allows common users and engineers to configure agents using agnostic model selection.
    • Supports multiple deployment patterns including top-level agent platforms and forward-deployed engineering support.
    • Enables webhook and non-human triggers for event-based agent execution.
  • Examples:
    • Connecting agents to different data systems using MCP connectors.
    • Triggering agents via Microsoft Teams, Slack, or webhooks without human intervention.
  • Terminology:
    • Agnostic models
    • Rag knowledge
    • MCP connectors
    • Workflow functionality
    • Agent skills
    • Context windows
  • Why it matters: Provides technical depth on how enterprise software companies can scale agentic solutions across diverse customer stacks.

Data Layers, Ontologies, and Context Management

  • Explanation: Discussing the challenges of messy data, data layers, ontologies, and managing context windows across disparate clinical trial systems.
  • Key claims:
    • Data fragmentation across 13+ systems creates heavy cognitive load for humans.
    • Building an AI data layer aligns all systems into a common ontology to simplify querying and recommendations.
    • Managing context windows and pre-filtering data prevents LLM hallucinations and latency.
  • Examples:
    • Mapping disparate clinical terms like 'participant' across 13 systems to a unified ontology.
    • Pre-filtering tool lists using smaller sub-models before calling heavy LLMs.
  • Terminology:
    • Data layer
    • Ontology
    • Vectorize
    • Sub-model
    • Context window
    • GCP (Good Clinical Practice)
  • Why it matters: Addresses the fundamental data engineering hurdles required to make enterprise agents accurate and reliable.

Human-in-the-Loop and Evaluation Frameworks

  • Explanation: Exploring the role of human oversight, benchmarking, and evaluation mechanisms to ensure agent outputs remain accurate and compliant.
  • Key claims:
    • Human-in-the-loop ensures trust and accuracy in high-stakes clinical trial decisions.
    • Evaluations test whether agents achieve expected intents, follow design specifications, and adhere to GXP standards.
    • Benchmarking configurations against test evidence ensures consistent agent performance.
  • Examples:
    • Reviewing agent classification corrections against human inputs to calculate deltas.
    • Benchmarking different GPT and Claude configurations for accuracy.
  • Terminology:
    • Evaluation harness
    • Benchmarking
    • GXP compliant
    • Delta
    • Ground truth
  • Why it matters: Crucial for regulated industries where mistakes can invalidate clinical trials or compromise patient safety.

Key Points

Solving Cognitive Load Limits

  • Explanation: Human workers in clinical trials face massive cognitive loads, reading 200+ page protocols and navigating 13 disparate systems.
  • Evidence: Clinical trials involve thousands of documents per month per study and strict regulatory oversight.
  • Practical implication: Agentic AI acts as a connective tissue, absorbing the heavy data-processing burden and providing actionable recommendations.

Platform Approach to Agent Building

  • Explanation: Medable provides both a platform and an experience, enabling internal teams and customers to build custom agents on top of core capabilities.
  • Evidence: A customer built a full Microsoft Teams agent ecosystem in a 70-minute session using Medable connectors.
  • Practical implication: Platform flexibility accelerates product delivery cycles and empowers non-technical users to configure domain-specific agents.

The Necessity of Data Ontologies

  • Explanation: Without a unified ontology, agents struggle to query fragmented data sources effectively.
  • Evidence: Different clinical systems use different terminology for the same concepts (e.g., participant vs. patient).
  • Practical implication: Investing in an AI data layer that maps data to a common ontology drastically improves agent accuracy.

Frameworks, Models & Processes

Agent Studio Platform Model

  • How it works: Provides foundational agent primitives (models, MCP connectors, workflow, triggers) that power both custom applications and customer-built agents.
  • Components:
    • Agnostic model support
    • MCP connectors for data systems
    • Workflow functionality
    • Agent skills
    • Multiple trigger types (chat, webhook, integrations)
  • When to use: When scaling AI agent development across multiple enterprise workflows and custom customer use cases.

Human-in-the-Loop Evaluation Framework

  • How it works: Combines automated agent outputs with human review loops to measure deltas, evaluate correctness, and continuously improve agent accuracy.
  • Components:
    • Ground truth comparison
    • Automated benchmarking against configurations
    • Human review and correction logging
    • Iterative prompt and model tuning
  • When to use: In highly regulated environments like clinical trials where error rates must be strictly monitored and minimized.

Examples & Case Studies

A customer with business-side background onboarded with Medable for 40 minutes, stepped away for a month, and returned having built their own ecosystem of Microsoft Teams agents using Medable connectors.

  • Illustrates: The usability and power of a well-designed agent platform.
  • Lesson: When foundational primitives and connectors are well-built, non-technical domain experts can rapidly build complex agent workflows.

Processing over 2,000 to 80,000 clinical documents through ETMF agents to assign metadata classifications.

  • Illustrates: Automating heavy manual administrative overhead in clinical trials.
  • Lesson: Agents drastically reduce the time auditors spend searching for trial records.

Actionable Takeaways

  • Immediate:
    • Recognize the distinction between raw LLM prompting and structured agent platforms.
    • Map out data fragmentation before attempting multi-system agent workflows.
    • Implement evaluation harnesses early to track agent accuracy.
  • Strategic:
    • Adopt a platform approach to agent development to empower both internal teams and customers.
    • Focus AI adoption on reducing administrative operational burdens in high-friction industries.
    • Treat human-in-the-loop workflows as a continuous improvement loop rather than a static check.
  • Questions to investigate:
    • How do you effectively manage context window limitations when agents span 13+ external systems?
    • What is the optimal balance between autonomous agent execution and human oversight in GXP-compliant environments?
    • How can ontologies be dynamically updated as new data structures emerge?

Claims Worth Verifying

  • It currently takes over 10 years to bring a drug to market. (Statistical / Industry norm)
  • Single clinical studies can produce tens of thousands of documents per month. (Operational statistic)

Notable Quotes

"Welcome to Just Now Possible with Teresa Torres." (at 0:04) "We're a SaaS platform company from the very beginning. We've always solved our solutions from a platform approach." (at 27:30)

Compressed Summary

  • Medable's Agent Studio enables internal teams and customers to build agentic clinical trial workflows.
  • Clinical trials suffer from heavy administrative burdens and fragmented data across 13+ disparate systems.
  • A unified AI data layer and ontology are critical for accurate multi-system agent querying.
  • Human-in-the-loop evaluation frameworks ensure GXP compliance and build trust in regulated environments.
  • Keywords: agentic ai, clinical trials, agent platform, ontology, evaluation framework
  • Core insight: Building successful enterprise AI agents requires a robust platform architecture, unified data ontologies, and rigorous human-in-the-loop evaluation frameworks.

title: Building Agent Studio: How Medable Is Using Agentic AI to Accelerate Clinical Trials
